conceptual assets.concept: Buffered FIFO contents (queued data stored in the FIFO memory/register)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL implements storage and later readback of enqueued words: write processes assign the input word into storage under the write decision (e.g. "if (we = '1') then fifo_mem(to_integer(unsigned(w_pnt(w_pnt'left-1 downto 0)))) <= wdata_i;" for depth>1 and "fifo_reg <= wdata_i;" for depth=1). Read paths drive the output from storage (e.g. "rdata_o <= fifo_mem(to_integer(unsigned(r_pnt_ff(r_pnt_ff'left-1 downto 0))))" in the async case or the registered-read assignment in the sync case). Reads and system behavior depend on the stored values, so integrity of the stored FIFO contents matters. The memory/register are the stores, wdata_i is the setting input, and rdata_o is the module exit for this value.

conceptual assets.concept: Enqueue/dequeue decision signals that determine when writes and reads occur
conceptual assets.reasoning: The entity computes internal write/read enables which control pointer increments and memory updates: "re <= re_i when (FIFO_SAFE = false) else (re_i and avail);" and "we <= we_i when (FIFO_SAFE = false) else (we_i and free);". Pointer next values and memory writes/reads are gated by these signals (w_nxt/r_nxt update when we/re = '1', and write/read processes execute only when we/re = '1'). Corruption of these decisions would violate the implemented enqueue/dequeue behavior. The internal signals we/re compute the decision; the inputs we_i/re_i are the setting points.

conceptual assets.concept: Pointer state (write and read pointers) that determines where data is written/read and underpins occupancy calculations
conceptual assets.reasoning: Pointer registers hold the enqueue/dequeue indices and are updated on clock edges: the pointer_reg process sets w_pnt/r_pnt from w_nxt/r_nxt with reset to zero ("if (rstn_i = '0') then w_pnt <= (others => '0'); r_pnt <= (others => '0'); elsif rising_edge(clk_i) then w_pnt <= w_nxt; r_pnt <= r_nxt;"). Memory writes index fifo_mem using the lower bits of w_pnt and reads index using r_pnt or r_pnt_ff; full/empty and level are computed from pointer bits. Thus pointer integrity is required for correct addressing, ordering and occupancy. The stored pointer registers are the realization points (including the registered async-read pointer r_pnt_ff used for asynchronous data reads).

conceptual assets.concept: Occupancy and status indicators (level, free/avail/half and their exported ports) that report FIFO fullness/availability
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL computes an occupancy count and derived status signals: "level <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(w_pnt) - unsigned(r_pnt));" which is mapped to the 32-bit output in level_extend; "half <= level(level'left-1) or full"; "free <= not full"; "avail <= not empty". These status signals are exported (either directly in the async path: "free_o <= free; avail_o <= avail; half_o <= half;" or registered in the FIFO_RSYNC path via sync_status). System behavior and gating (e.g. FIFO_SAFE gating of we/re) depend on these indicators, so their integrity matters. level/free/avail/half compute the occupancy semantics; level_o/free_o/avail_o/half_o are their exit ports.
